items.title: [FDD Diary #19] Manual Testing Hell
content:
Manual testing isn't a time problem.
It's a willpower problem.

Fifth check, focus drops.
Tenth, skimming.
Twentieth, you stop looking.

That's exactly the door bugs walk through.

Changed the notification text.
Check everything. Login. Agent. Settings.
Thirty minutes.

Another fix. Everything again. Thirty minutes.
Another fix. Thirty minutes.

'This one probably didn't break.'
Skip it.

Dead cat stays in the box.

Fifty features. Fifty boxes to open.

Don't want to? 'Probably fine.' Skip.

Gets discovered later.
At the worst possible moment.
Always.

Needed a way out.

items.title: [FDD Diary #20] Before Tests
content:
Changed one line. Notification text. Tiny fix.
Pushed it.

Dashboard broke. Settings broke. Agent log stopped.

One line. Three things I didn't touch.
No way to know before pushing.

AI said: 'Write tests.'

Tests are code. I don't write code.

'A test is writing down: if this works, it's done.'

Wait.

Spec: 'Login shows dashboard.' That's the goal.
Test: 'Click login. Dashboard appears.' That's the proof.

I write the bar. AI writes the code.

Write the bar before the code. Not after.

'Notification fires once.'
'Settings save correctly.'

Plain language. Hand it to the AI.
AI writes the test code.

Decisions are mine.
Implementation is the AI's.
Verification is the test's.

items.title: [FDD Diary #21] 6,260 Safety Nets
content:
Five tests became fifty.
Fifty became five hundred.
Five hundred became 6,260.

Run them all. One minute. Every feature checked.

Changed code. Something break?
Thirty seconds. The answer's there.

'Can I delete this function?'
Run tests. All pass. Yes.

'Can I restructure this?'
Three fail. Fix three. Run again. All pass. Yes.

Too scared to touch code before.
Now I cut without hesitation.

Tests aren't verification.
They're courage.

All 6,260 passed. Pushed to production.
69 issues in the real world.

Tests only check what I thought of.

But those 69? Not panic. A list.
Fixed one by one. Added a test each time.
6,260 became 6,329.

Not perfect. 6,260 times better than nothing.
